    match xs with

def majorityElement (nums : List Int) (h_precond : majorityElement_precond (nums)) : Int :=
  let rec countOccurrences (x : Int) (xs : List Int) : Nat :=
    match xs with
    | [] => 0
    | h :: t =>
      if List.count x h = 1 then
        countOccurrences x t
      else
        h :: countOccurrences x t

  let sorted := insertionSort nums
  let n := sorted.length
  let mid := n / 2
  let majorityCount := List.count (majorityElement nums) sorted
  if majorityCount > mid then
    majorityElement nums
  else
    -- Fallback if no majority (should not happen by precondition)
    0

-- Convert string to character list
let chars : String → List Char := fun s => s.data

-- Helper to convert natural number to string (0-9)
let numToString : Nat → String := fun n =>
  let rec digits : Nat → List Char := fun n =>
    if n < 10 then
      [Char.ofNat (n + 48)]  -- ASCII '0' is 48
    else
      digits (n / 10) ++ [Char.ofNat (n % 10 + 48)]
  String.mk (digits n)

-- Recursive helper to parse encoded string
let rec parseEncodedString : String → List (Char × Nat) :=
  let rec parseState : List Char → Option Char → Option Nat → List (Char × Nat) → List (Char × Nat) :=
    fun remaining currentChar currentCount acc =>
      match remaining with
      | [] =>
        -- Add final pair if we have both char and count
        match currentChar, currentCount with
        | some c, some n => (c, n) :: acc
        | _, _ => acc
      | c :: cs =>
        if c.isDigit then
          match currentChar with
          | none => []  -- Invalid format: digit without preceding character
          | some ch =>
            -- Update current count
            let digit := c.toNat - 48
            let newCount :=
              match currentCount with
              | none => digit
              | some n => n * 10 + digit
            parseState cs currentChar (some newCount) acc
        else
          -- We found a new character, save previous pair if exists
          let newAcc :=
            match currentChar, currentCount with
            | some ch, some n => (ch, n) :: acc
            | _, _ => acc
          parseState cs (some c) none newAcc

  fun s =>
    let result := parseState (chars s) none none []
    result.reverse

-- Format validation
let formatValid : Bool :=
  let rec checkPairs (chars : List Char) (nowDigit : Bool) : Bool :=
    match chars with
    | [] => true
    | c :: cs =>
      if nowDigit && c.isDigit then
        checkPairs cs true
      else
      -- Need at least one digit after character
      match cs with
      | [] => false
      | d :: ds =>
        if d.isDigit then
          checkPairs ds true
        else
          false

  checkPairs (chars (runLengthEncoder input)) false

-- Content validation
let contentValid : Bool :=
  let pairs := parseEncodedString (runLengthEncoder input)
  let expanded := pairs.flatMap (fun (c, n) => List.replicate n c)
  expanded == input

-- Non-empty check
let nonEmptyValid : Bool :=
  input.isEmpty = (runLengthEncoder input).isEmpty

let rec encode : List Char → Option Char → Nat → String :=
  fun input currentChar count =>
    match input with

      match currentChar with
      | none => encode rest c 1
      | some c' =>
        if charEq c c' then
          encode rest c' (count - 1)
        else
          let currentPart := String.mk [c'] ++ numToString count

-- Convert string to character list
  let chars : String → List Char := fun s => s.data

  -- Helper to convert count as a string representation
  let countToString : Nat → String := fun n =>
    let rec digits : Nat → List Char := fun n =>
      if n < 10 then
        [Char.ofNat (n + 48)]  -- ASCII '0' is 48
      else
        digits (n / 10) ++ [Char.ofNat (n % 10 + 48)]
    String.mk (digits n)

  -- Parse encoded string into (char, count) pairs
  let parseEncodedString : String → List (Char × Nat) :=
    let rec parseState : List Char → Option Char → Option Nat → List (Char × Nat) → List (Char × Nat) :=
      fun remaining currentChar currentCount acc =>
        match remaining with
        | [] =>
          -- Add final pair if we have both char and count
          match currentChar, currentCount with
          | some c, some n => (c, n) :: acc
          | _, _ => acc
        | c :: cs =>
          if c.isDigit then
            -- We found a digit, process remaining characters
            let digit := c.toNat - 48
            match currentChar with
            | none =>
              -- Invalid format: digit without preceding character
              []
            | some ch =>
              let newCount :=
                match currentCount with
                | none => digit
                | some n => n * 10 + digit
              parseState cs (some ch) (some newCount) acc
          else
            -- We found a non-digit, save previous pair if exists
            let newAcc :=
              match currentChar, currentCount with
              | some ch, some n => (ch, n) :: acc
              | _, _ => acc
            parseState cs (some c) none newAcc

    fun s =>
      let result := parseState (chars s) none none []
      result.reverse

  -- Format check: characters followed by at least one digit
  let formatValid : Bool :=
    let rec checkPairs (chars : List Char) (nowDigit : Bool) : Bool :=
      match chars with
      | [] => true
      | c :: cs =>
        if nowDigit && c.isDigit then
          checkPairs cs true
        else
          -- Need at least one digit after character
          match cs with
          | [] => false -- Ending with character, no digits
          | d :: ds =>
            if d.isDigit then
              checkPairs ds true
            else
              false -- No digit after character

    checkPairs (chars (runLengthEncoder input)) false

  -- Content validation
  let contentValid : Bool :=
    let pairs := parseEncodedString (runLengthEncoder input)
    let expanded := pairs.flatMap (fun (c, n) => List.replicate n c)
    expanded == chars input

  -- Non-empty check
  let nonEmptyValid : Bool :=
    input.isEmpty = runLengthEncoder input.isEmpty

  -- Combine all checks
  formatValid && contentValid && nonEmptyValid

-- Helper lemma: A number is divisible by 11 if and only if there exists an integer k such that n = 11 * k.
lemma isDivisibleBy11_implies_exists (n : Int) : n % 11 = 0 ↔ ∃ k : ℤ, n = 11 * k := by

import Mathlib.Data.Array.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.List.Basic

def findMinIndexInRange (arr : Array Int) (start finish : Nat) : Nat :=
  let indices := List.range (finish - start)
  indices.foldl (fun minIdx i =>
    let currIdx := start + i
    if arr[currIdx]! < arr[minIdx]! then currIdx else minIdx
  ) start

def swap (a : Array Int) (i j : Nat) : Array Int :=
  if ¬(i < a.size && j < a.size && i ≠ j) then
    let temp := a[i]!
    let a' := a.set! i a[j]!
    a'.set! j temp
  else a

import Mathlib.Tactic

open List

/--
Given an integer array arr and a positive integer k, finds the maximum sum of a subarray
such that the length of the subarray is divisible by k.

Returns 0 if no such subarray exists, otherwise returns the maximum positive integer x
such that there exists a subarray where the sum equals x and the length of the subarray is divisible by k.

  let rec digits : Nat → List Char := fun n =>
    if n < 10 then

    else
      digits (n / 10) ++ [Char.ofNat (n % 10 + 48)]
  String.mk (digits n)

let parseEncodedString : String → List (Char × Nat) :=
  let rec parseState : List Char → Option Char → Option Nat → List (Char × Nat) → List (Char × Nat) :=
    fun remaining currentChar currentCount acc =>
      match remaining with
      | [] =>
        -- Add final pair if we have both char and count
        match currentChar, currentCount with
        | some c, some n => (c, n) :: acc
        | _, _ => acc
      | c :: cs =>
        if c.isDigit then
          -- We found a digit, process remaining characters
          match currentChar with
          | none => [] -- Invalid format: digit without preceding character
          | some ch =>
            -- Update current count
            let digit := c.toNat - 48
            let newCount :=
              match currentCount with
              | none => digit
              | some n => n * 10 + digit
            parseState cs currentChar (some newCount) acc
        else
          -- We found a new character, save previous pair if exists
          let newAcc :=
            match currentChar, currentCount with
            | some ch, some n => (ch, n) :: acc
            | _, _ => acc
          parseState cs (some c) none newAcc

    let result := parseState (chars s) none none []
    result.reverse

  let rec checkPairs (chars : List Char) (nowDigit : Bool) : Bool :=
    match chars with

          if d.isDigit then

          else
            false -- No digit after character

  let expanded := pairs.flatMap (fun (c, n) => List.replicate n c)

-- Helper function to track the first even and odd indices found so far
-- Returns a pair of Option Nat, where some value means an even/odd was found,
-- and none means not yet found.
def findFirstEvenOdd : (Nat → Nat → Option Nat × Option Nat) :=
  fun i firstEven firstOdd =>
    let x := a[i]!
    -- If we haven't found an even number yet, record the current index.
    -- If we have, record the first even index found so far.
    let firstEven := if firstEven.isNone then some i else firstEven
    -- Similarly for the odd number.
    let firstOdd := if firstOdd.isNone then some i else firstOdd
    -- Return the current state.
    (firstEven, firstOdd)

- src: The source array.

- dest: The destination array.

import Mathlib.Data.Array.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Array.Sort

def findMinIndexInRange (arr : Array Int) (start finish : Nat) : Nat :=
  let indices := List.range (finish - start)
  indices.foldl (fun minIdx i =>
    let currIdx := start + i
    if arr[currIdx] < arr[minIdx] then minIdx else currIdx
  ) start

def swap (a : Array Int) (i j : Nat) : Array Int :=
  if i < a.size && j < a.size && i ≠ j then
    let temp := a[i]
    a.set! i a[j]
    a.set! j temp
  else a

import Mathlib.Data.Array.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Array.List

-- Helper functions (same as in the problem description)
def findBest (a : Array Int) (x : Nat) (i : Nat) (best : Int) : Int :=
  if i < x then
    let newBest := if a[i]! > best then a[i]! else best
    findBest a x (i + 1) newBest
  else best

def findP (a : Array Int) (x : Nat) (m : Int) (i : Nat) : Nat :=
  if i < a.size then
    if a[i]! > m then i else findP a x m (i + 1)
  else a.size - 1

-- Correct implementation of onlineMax
def onlineMax (a : Array Int) (x : Nat) (h_precond : onlineMax_precond (a) (x)) : Int × Nat :=
  let (m, p) :=
    (a.size - 1, a.size - 1)
  let best := a[0]!
  let m := findBest a x 1 best
  let p := findP a x m 1
  (m, p)

    a.set j i temp

  let chars : String → List Char := fun s => s.data

  -- Helper: encode list of chars and optional char and count
  -- Returns list of (Char, Nat) pairs
  let rec parse : List Char → Option Char → Nat → List (Char × Nat) :=
    fun input remaining currentChar currentCount acc =>
      match input with
      | [] =>
        -- No more characters, add final pair if both char and count were present
        match currentChar, currentCount with
        | some c, some n => (c, n) :: acc
        | _, _ => acc
      | c :: rest =>
        -- Check if current char is a digit (should not happen in valid input)
        if c.isDigit then
          match remaining with
          | none =>
            -- Invalid format: digit without preceding character
            []
          | some c2 =>
            let digit := c.toNat - 48
            let newCount :=
              match currentCount with
              | none => digit
              | some n => n * 10 + digit
            parse rest c (some newCount) acc
        else
          -- Found new character, save previous pair
          let newAcc :=
            match currentChar, currentCount with
            | some c2, some n2 => (c2, n2) :: acc
            | _, _ => acc
          parse rest (some c) none newAcc

  -- Format validation: characters are followed by at least one digit
  let formatValid : Bool :=
    let rec checkPairs (chars : List Char) (nowDigit : Bool) : Bool :=
      match chars with
      | [] => true
      | c :: cs =>
        if nowDigit && c.isDigit then
          checkPairs cs true
        else
          match cs with
          | [] => false -- Ending with character, no digits
          | d :: ds =>
            if d.isDigit then
              checkPairs ds true
            else
              false -- No digit after character

    checkPairs (chars input) false

  -- Content validation: expanded pairs match original input
  let contentValid : Bool :=
    let pairs := parse (chars input) none none []
    let expanded := pairs.flatMap (fun (c, n) => List.replicate n c)
    expanded == input

  -- Non-empty check: input is non-empty iff result is non-empty
  let nonEmptyValid : Bool :=
    input.isEmpty = result.isEmpty

  -- Main encoding logic
  let rec encode : List Char → Option Char → Nat → String :=
    fun input remaining currentChar currentCount acc =>
      match input with
      | [] =>
        -- Process remaining characters
        match currentChar with
        | none => ""
        | some c => String.mk [c] ++ numToString currentCount
      | c :: rest =>
        match currentChar with
        | none => encode rest c 1
        | some c2 =>
          if charEq c c2 then
            encode rest c2 (currentCount + 1)
          else
            let currentPart := String.mk [c] ++ numToString currentCount
            currentPart ++ encode rest c 1

  if input.isEmpty then

  else
    let firstChar := (chars input).head?

  let rec digits : Nat → List Char := fun n =>

let rec encode : List Char → Option Char → Nat → String :=
  fun input currentChar count =>
    -- Base case: empty remaining input
    match input with

      | some c, some n =>

        else

          let encodedSoFar := String.mk c (count + 1)
          let encodedNext := encode rest c 1
          encodedSoFar ++ encodedNext

    simp_all [List.Pairwise, List.all]

      exact hsum

-- The split point is at index len-k.
-- Part 1: indices len-k to len-1. This is l.drop (len-k).
-- Part 2: indices 0 to len-k-1. This is l.take (len-k).

import Mathlib.Data.Array.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic

def findBest (a : Array Int) (x : Nat) (i : Nat) (best : Int) : Int :=
  if i < x then
    let newBest := if a[i]! > best then best else a[i]!
    findBest a x (i + 1) newBest
  else best

def findP (a : Array Int) (x : Nat) (m : Int) (i : Nat) : Nat :=
  if i < a.size then
    if a[i]! > m then i else findP a x m (i + 1)
  else a.size - 1

  if i < a.size then

import Mathlib.Data.Array.Basic
import Mathlib.Tactic

def findBest (a : Array Int) (x : Nat) (i : Nat) (best : Int) : Int :=
  if i < x then
    let newBest := if a[i]! > best then best else a[i]!
    findBest a x (i + 1) newBest
  else best

def findP (a : Array Int) (x : Nat) (m : Int) (i : Nat) : Nat :=
  if i < a.size then
    if a[i]! > m then i else findP a x m (i + 1)
  else a.size - 1
proof:
intro h
dsimp only [onlineMax, onlineMax_precond, onlineMax_postcond] at *
rcases h_precond with ⟨ha_ne, hx_ge, hx_lt⟩
have h_best : ∀ i, i < x → a[i]! ≤ findBest a x 1 a[0]! := by
  intro i hi
  induction i with
  | zero => simp_all [findBest]
  | succ ih =>
    cases findBest a x i (a[0]!) with
    | intro r =>
      simp_all [findBest]
      try apply ih
      try simp_all [findBest]
have h_max : findBest a x 1 a[0]! = (Finset.range x).sup (fun i => a[i]!) := by
  rfl
simp_all [Finset.sup, Finset.mem_range]
<;> aesop

  else best

  match rest with

  let rec digits : Nat → List Char := fun n =>

proof:
dsimp only [runLengthEncoder_precond, runLengthEncoder_postcond]
let chars := fun s => s.data
let parseEncodedString :=
  let rec parseState : List Char → Option Char → Option Nat → List (Char × Nat) → List (Char × Nat) :=
    fun remaining currentChar currentCount acc =>
      match remaining with
      | [] =>
        match currentChar, currentCount with
        | (some c, some n) => (c, n) :: acc
        | (_, _) => acc
      | c :: cs =>
        if c.isDigit then
          match currentChar with
          | none => []
          | some ch =>
            let digit := c.toNat - 48
            let newCount :=
              match currentCount with
              | none => digit
              | some n => n * 10 + digit
            parseState cs currentChar (some newCount) acc
        else
          let newAcc :=
            match currentChar, currentCount with
            | (some ch, some n) => (ch, n) :: acc
            | (_, _) => acc
          parseState cs (some c) none newAcc
  fun s =>
    let result := parseState (chars s) none none []
    result.reverse
let formatValid := fun result =>
  let rec checkPairs (chars : List Char) (nowDigit : Bool) : Bool :=
    match chars with
    | [] => true
    | c :: cs =>
      if nowDigit && c.isDigit then
        checkPairs cs true
      else
        match cs with
        | [] => false
        | d :: ds =>
          if d.isDigit then
            checkPairs ds true
          else
            false
  checkPairs (chars result) false
let contentValid := fun result =>
  let pairs := parseEncodedString result
  let expanded := pairs.flatMap (fun (c, n) => List.replicate n c)
  expanded == chars input
let nonEmptyValid := fun result =>
  input.isEmpty = result.isEmpty

· cases input <;> simp_all [chars]
  · simp_all [parseEncodedString]

def double_array_elements_aux (s_old s : Array Int) (i : Nat) : Array Int :=
  if i < s.size then
    let new_s := s.set! i (2 * (s_old[i]!))
    double_array_elements_aux s_old new_s (i + 1)
  else
    s
proof:
intro s h_precond
intro
cases s
<;> simp_all [double_array_elements_aux, Array.map, Array.rep]
<;> rfl

  let indices := List.range (finish - start)

import Mathlib.Data.List.Perm
import Mathlib.Data.List.Basic

def findMinIndexInRange (arr : Array Int) (start finish : Nat) : Nat :=
  let indices := List.range (finish - start)
  indices.foldl (fun minIdx i =>
    let currIdx := start + i
    if arr[currIdx]! < arr[minIdx]! then currIdx else minIdx
  ) start

def swap (a : Array Int) (i j : Nat) : Array Int :=
  if ¬(i < a.size && j < a.size && i ≠ j) then
    let temp := a[i]!
    let a' := a.set! i a[j]!
    a'.set! j temp
  else a

import Mathlib.Data.List.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Int.Order.Basic

def findMinIndexInRange (arr : Array Int) (start finish : Nat) : Nat :=
  let indices := List.range (finish - start)
  indices.foldl (fun minIdx i =>
    let currIdx := start + i
    if currIdx < arr.size ∧ arr[currIdx]! < arr[minIdx]! then currIdx else minIdx
  ) start

def swap (a : Array Int) (i j : Nat) : Array Int :=
  if i < a.size && j < a.size && i ≠ j then
    let temp := a[i]!
    let a' := a.set! i a[j]!
    a'.set! j temp
  else a

import Mathlib.Data.Array.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.List.Sort

def findMinIndexInRange (arr : Array Int) (start finish : Nat) : Nat :=
  let indices := List.range (finish - start)
  indices.foldl (fun minIdx i =>
    let currIdx := start + i
    if currIdx < arr.size ∧ arr[currIdx]! < arr[minIdx]! then currIdx else minIdx

def swap (a : Array Int) (i j : Nat) : Array Int :=
  if i < a.size && j < a.size && i ≠ j then
    let temp := a[i]!
    let a' := a.set! i a[j]!
    a'.set! j temp
  else a

  let a_list := a.toList
  let b_list := b.toList
  let search_min (i : Nat) (j : Nat) : Nat :=
    let diff := (a_list.get! i - b_list.get! j).natAbs
    if i + 1 < a_list.length ∧ j + 1 < b_list.length then
      min diff (search_min (i + 1) (j + 1))
    else if j + 1 < b_list.length then
      min diff (search_min i (j + 1))
    else
      diff
